name: xcdat
baseline: marisa-trie (LOUDS nested patricia trie, s-yata/marisa-trie); also compared against tx LOUDS trie, fst, pdt
workload: Static string dictionary lookup (key to ID) and decode (ID to key) on English Wikipedia titles (14,130,439 keys, 285 MiB), IPAdic, Askitis Distinct and Url datasets; 1,000 random query keys, best of 10 runs.
claimed_speedup: Wiki dataset lookup: xcdat<8> 826 ns/key vs marisa 1818 ns/key (about 2.2x faster, derived from page data); xcdat<15> 619 ns/key vs 1818 (about 2.9x, derived). Decode: xcdat<8> 1173 ns/id vs marisa 1515 ns/id. Url dataset lookup: xcdat<8> 469 vs marisa 1789 ns/key. Memory cost: xcdat<8> 139 MiB vs marisa 69 MiB on Wiki.
hardware: MacBook Pro 13-inch 2019, 2.4 GHz Quad-Core Intel Core i5, 16 GB 2133 MHz LPDDR3, macOS Catalina 10.15
tradeoffs: Faster than marisa but uses about 2x the memory on Wiki (139 vs 69 MiB) and up to 2x on other sets. Slower than darts-clone on lookup (450 ns/key on Wiki) but about 3.8x smaller (139 vs 525 MiB). Static dictionary only; header-only C++17; supports prefix and predictive search, 64-bit pointers and binary keys.
caveats: The baseline is marisa-trie, not SDSL or sux, so it is a trie-dictionary win rather than a bitvector or wavelet-tree win. Benchmark ran on a laptop Core i5 with a single macOS toolchain (CPU model number not given, only '2.4 GHz Quad-Core Intel Core i5'). Benchmark code lives in the sibling repo kampersanda/fast_succinct_trie/bench (opened as a link only; the numbers were read from the xcdat README). Author states a dastrie build failure on one dataset. Compared directly to a succinct trie incumbent, not to std containers.
found_via: GitHub: WebSearch 'github compact trie dictionary C++ marisa-trie xcdat benchmark succinct trie faster', then raw README at raw.githubusercontent.com/kampersanda/xcdat/HEAD/README.md

name: faster-minuter (wt_fbb fixed-block-boosting wavelet tree)
baseline: SDSL wavelet trees (e.g. Huffman-shaped and hybrid-bitvector wavelet trees inside SDSL FM-indexes)
workload: Wavelet tree plugged into an FM-index (the 'Faster Minuter' index) for count and locate queries; details only in the Algorithmica 2019 paper, which could not be opened here (publisher and arXiv hosts blocked).
claimed_speedup: No numbers on the repo page. The paper title 'Fixed Block Compression Boosting in FM-Indexes: Theory and Practice' (Algorithmica 81(4), 2019) is cited by the README for the experimental evaluation. A search snippet from a third-party paper only says wt-fbb 'performs fastest' in its comparison; no ratio seen.
tradeoffs: SDSL-compatible class wt_fbb; default hybrid bitvector, faster but larger bitvectors can be plugged in. Tested on Linux/PC only. Header-only include directory.
caveats: Could not read the paper, so the size of the win over SDSL is unverified; verifier should open the Algorithmica paper (or a copy) and, if the win holds against SDSL, retier to B. last_commit not shown on the repo page; the GitHub topics page listed the repo as updated May 18, 2021, so maintenance_status is inferred. Repo has no benchmark scripts.
found_via: GitHub: https://github.com/topics/wavelet-tree?l=c%2B%2B; README via raw.githubusercontent.com; WebSearch snippet for the paper

name: pwm (parallel wavelet tree and wavelet matrix construction)
baseline: Other published wavelet tree construction algorithms, including SDSL-based construction (optional PWM_BUILD_SDSL_WT competitor build)
workload: Construction of wavelet trees and wavelet matrices from text, sequential, shared-memory parallel and (semi-)external memory variants; the repo bundles competitor implementations for comparison.
claimed_speedup: No numbers on the repo page. README says a detailed description and benchmarks are in the ALENEX 2018 paper 'Simple, Fast and Lightweight Parallel Wavelet Tree Construction' (Fischer, Kurpicz, Lobel); paper not opened.
tradeoffs: Construction only, not query speed. Parallel variants need many cores; some competitors need Cilk (gcc < 8) and the SDSL competitor build is off by default.
caveats: Evidence is the peer-reviewed ALENEX paper (would be tier B if the win over SDSL construction is confirmed), but it could not be opened in this environment. Whether SDSL is among the beaten baselines is inferred from the repo's PWM_BUILD_SDSL_WT option and unconfirmed. last_commit not shown; topics page listed the repo as updated Jun 27, 2023.
